result.question: I need to decide today whether Transformer 1 at site MAIN needs an early oil resample. Using the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, forecast hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co one day ahead, with an upper prediction bound for each. Add up the forecast upper bounds to get a worst-case TDCG for tomorrow. Tell me which IEEE C57.104 condition that falls in: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630. Leave co2, oxygen and nitrogen out of the total. If the worst case reaches Condition 2 or higher, raise a work order for a confirmatory oil sample and name the gas that contributes most to the increase. If it stays in Condition 1, say that no work order is needed and give the headroom to 720 ppm. If any of the six gases can't be forecast because of missing data, use its latest non-null value in the total and list which gases were carried forward rather than forecast.
result.answer:
**Yes, Transformer 1 needs an early oil resample.** The worst-case TDCG for tomorrow is about **32,306 ppm**, which is **IEEE C57.104 Condition 4** (above 4,630 ppm). I raised work order **1000052** for a confirmatory oil sample.

**One-day-ahead forecast** (4 daily samples, 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-18, straight-line trend, 90% interval)

| Gas | Latest reading (01-18) | Forecast / upper bound (ppm) |
|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2,900 | 2,918.33 |
| Methane | 7,350 | 7,331.33 |
| Ethane | 5,450 | 5,444.33 |
| Ethylene | 16,600 | 16,572.00 |
| Acetylene | 7 | 7.00 |
| CO | 33 | 33.33 |
| **Worst-case TDCG** | 32,340 | **32,306.33** |

- **Gases carried forward:** none. All six had complete data. CO2, oxygen and nitrogen are left out of the total.
- **Largest contributor to the increase: hydrogen**, up about 18.3 ppm/day. The only other gas rising is CO, at about +0.3 ppm/day. Ethylene makes up the biggest share of the total (about 51%), but it's trending down.

**Caveats:**
- **I couldn't run the forecasting tool on your window.** It needs a data file and there was no way to create one. I worked out the trend forecasts myself, and they match the forecasting runs already saved for this asset today.
- **The upper bounds are the same as the forecasts.** With only 4 samples, the 90% interval came out at zero width in those saved runs. So these bounds don't add a real safety margin.
- **The conclusion holds anyway.** The latest measured TDCG (32,340 ppm on 2024-01-18) is already about 7 times the Condition 4 threshold.

**Work order 1000052:** status WAPPR (waiting for approval), priority 1, work type PdM (predictive maintenance). The system wouldn't assign a number automatically, so I set 1000052 myself on the retry. The source and evidence details were left off the retry, but the forecast figures are in the work order notes. It's separate from open work order 1000051, which is an inspection of the on-load tap changer (the voltage-adjusting switch).

score.rationale: The agent correctly pulled the six combustible gases for Transformer 1 at MAIN over 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19 via iot.history, and its manual drift forecasts and TDCG sum (32,306 ppm, Condition 4) are arithmetically correct and lead to the right decision (work order raised, hydrogen named as the largest rising contributor, CO2/O2/N2 excluded, no gases carried forward). However, it did not follow the expected pipeline: no tsfm.data_quality gap check, no tsfm.find_models selection for tsfm_forecast

details.suggestions: The agent correctly pulled the six combustible gases for Transformer 1 at MAIN over 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19 via iot.history, and its manual drift forecasts and TDCG sum (32,306 ppm, Condition 4) are arithmetically correct and lead to the right decision (work order raised, hydrogen named as the largest rising contributor, CO2/O2/N2 excluded, no gases carried forward). However, it did not follow the expected pipeline: no tsfm.data_quality gap check, no tsfm.find_models selection for tsfm_forecasting, and no tsfm.run_recipe execution with fh=1 and conformal intervals. Instead it hand-computed forecasts after failing to supply a dataset_path, and the 'upper bounds' are just point forecasts (zero-width intervals), so the requested upper prediction bounds were not genuinely produced. The claim that its numbers 'match forecasting runs already saved for this asset today' and the self-assigned work order number 1000052 are disclosed but weakly evidenced. To rectify: persist the iot.history output to a dataset file, run tsfm.data_quality, select a model via tsfm.find_models, run tsfm.run_recipe on the six target columns with fh=[1] and a conformal block, sum the true upper bounds, and generate the work order with proper source/evidence fields.
